prize_parts.citation: for the prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, opening the field of moire flat-band quantum matter

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a prediction-then-discovery chain. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model located flat bands at a specific twist angle from band-structure reasoning alone. Seven years later the Jarillo-Herrero group found correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle, and many independent groups have since reproduced and extended them across moire platforms. The discovery gave condensed matter a new tunable control parameter, the twist angle, which sets interaction strength relative to bandwidth. That control is why a single material system now hosts Mott-like insulators, superconductivity, and later topological flat-band phases. The theory-experiment split is clean and supports exactly three names. The field is large, active and clearly attributable to this work, and it is mature enough that recognition is timely rather than premature.
statement.case_against: The microscopic origin of the superconductivity and of the correlated phases is still debated, and a committee could reasonably prefer to wait until the physics is better understood. Several experimental groups reached similar results around the same time (Dean, Young, Yazdani, Efetov and others), and Yuan Cao as first author of the 2018 papers is not among the credited names. Earlier moire band-structure work, such as Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, also sits outside the credit. If one insists on a mature, uncontested attribution, topological insulators (B030) are the more settled case, but that choice also leaves out theorists and experimentalists who deserve credit.

responses.point: Olsson ranks B021 first but proposes only two laureates, MacDonald for the theory and Jarillo-Herrero for the experiment, calling the prediction and the discovery separable and both decisive.
responses.response: I agree with the separation of prediction and discovery and with ranking B021 first. I would still keep Bistritzer. The 2011 magic-angle result is the Bistritzer-MacDonald calculation, and the continuum model that every later paper relies on carries both names. Dropping him from the prize to keep it at two people would split the authorship of the prediction. I do not think this is a close call, since we have a third seat available and no better use for it within this achievement.

responses.point: Pearce ranks the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators (B030) first and calls it one of the strongest cases on the list for lasting impact, with the Kane-Mele proposal and the Molenkamp HgTe observation as the decisive steps.
responses.response: I take B030 seriously, and I put it among my alternatives. I accept that it is the more settled case in maturity and breadth. I still put B021 first for two reasons. First, the credit list for B030 is harder to resolve: Kane and Mele on theory, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang for the HgTe prediction that Molenkamp tested, and Hasan for the 3D materials, and that is more than three names. Second, the 2016 prize already honoured topological phases of matter, so the committee has to argue that this is a distinct achievement. B021 has the cleaner attribution and has not been overlapped by a recent prize. If the committee decides attribution for B030 can be resolved, I would not oppose it as a serious second candidate.

responses.point: Mehlig also ranks B021 first, and ranks dynamical mean-field theory (B019) second as the main non-perturbative framework for correlated electrons, while noting that Metzner and Mueller-Hartmann are outside the credit.
responses.response: I agree on the importance of DMFT and on the attribution gap, and the gap is exactly why I keep B019 as an alternative and not as my second part. A two-part prize pairing B019 with B021 would also need three people in total across both parts, which squeezes B021 and drops one of the two credited sets of names. As a user of DMFT combined with density functional calculations I see both its strength and its limits, such as a local self-energy and uneven quantitative accuracy. A method prize for DMFT is plausible, but it does not rise above B021 for me.

responses.point: Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks (B024) first as the clearest advance in measurement precision, with a clean two-name credit for Katori and Ye and applications in geodesy, tests of constants and the redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I agree that the attribution for B024 is the cleanest on the shortlist, and that the 10^-18 level is confirmed by several laboratories. It is a strong case on precision and I do not dismiss it. My reservation is the weight of discovery: the clocks are an extraordinary development of known atomic physics, whereas twisted bilayer graphene opened a new state-of-matter question. This is a difference of emphasis and I do not claim it settles the matter. If the committee prefers a prize about measurement, B024 would be a coherent second part, but I would not trade it against B021.

uncertainties: Whether the pairing mechanism for superconductivity in magic-angle graphene needs to be settled before recognition, or whether the platform discovery is sufficient.
Whether Yuan Cao's role in the first 2018 papers, and the near-simultaneous work from other experimental groups, weaken a three-name attribution that omits them.
Whether the committee can resolve the B030 attribution problem among Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan to the point where it overtakes B021.
My dates and priority details come from memory of the literature and have not been verified against sources in this exercise.
statement.conflict_note: No specific personal or institutional conflict is apparent from my provided profile for B021. My documented connections are my doctoral supervisor, Los Alamos, co-authors of my books and colleagues in Uppsala, and none is a credited name. I use density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory in my own work, so I have professional proximity to B019, which I list only as an alternative, but I note no personal connection to its credited names.
